# Native capture transactions

The dated implementation/delivery limits below retain their original checkpoint scope. On 4 October, an independent installed-app public-PCM run found that audio filenames had changed from released UTC microsecond stamps to capture UUIDs. The existing owner now observes the actual capture file and checks its released grammar and UTC capture interval; the assertion fails before the production repair and all forty-six transactions/218 states plus three native faults pass afterward. The canonical repaired bundle also matches immutable 1.6.0's complete final frame, post-exit History and exact WAV bytes in a real-Qwen paced capture. [Current capture/performance evidence](../../../../docs/verification/rust-release-performance/README.md) records the source/binary identities, negative control and bounded acceptance; physical microphone/global-key and complete-workflow checks remain open.

The reference is unchanged Mluva 1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. A temporary collector imports the external frozen release, verifies all imported application modules against that commit and invokes its actual application constructor, service initialization, capture/settings builders and preparation, ready, stop, cancel, completion and failure callbacks. [Released observations](released-capture-lifecycle.json) have SHA-256 `7b08d123d1d30a02e0d59711b18facfb3d2fe24eb5bf2e1ffc889fbbdfb1da97`.

The native comparison constructs the production `CapturePage`, `CaptureController`, `DesktopRuntime`, `CaptureSession`, `PipeWireRecorder`, speech clients and compatible SQLite stores. The microphone executable alone is replaced by a separate synthetic PCM process. Real loopback HTTP and WebSocket peers independently observe exact WAV uploads, multipart fields and audio/commit frames. Public GTK widgets and terminal callbacks expose results; no production test hook or interpreter is needed by the native test.

A second unchanged-release collection adds [22 compatible/local preview captures](released-capture-previews.json), SHA-256 `a20198541015f8b02ba97bd5c82da0fecfa3acc620070ab408856d5774a3bf5a`. The released constructor, builders and callbacks now run with actual compatible batch-preview or local preview sessions and the released local speech factory. Local assets are sparse readiness controls and inference is supplied by separate native peers. These additional 103 GTK states bring the joined comparison to 39 transactions and 184 observations. Compatible success, Incognito, cancellation and finalization failure followed by batch fallback match; Qwen 1.7B, Whisper Tiny and Parakeet v3 each match finalized capture, Incognito and cancellation on CPU and GPU protocol routes. Full results, History, exact audio and model requests, private modes, model process counts and temporary key removal match. Every Incognito terminal returns private memory-backed storage to its pre-capture state. Readiness labels retain the release's existing Scribe wording for compatible/local sessions.

A third collection joins actual Codex segment cleanup to the unchanged capture application. [Seven transactions](released-capture-segments.json), SHA-256 `1610063cc52756dc3660509f142fe4460e67ad5228519e5cf595b4caded6f226`, add 34 states, bringing the combined comparison to 46 transactions and 218 GTK observations. Full History/results and exact prepared prompts/process counts match for successful cleanup, unsafe-candidate fallback, bounded Stop, recording cancellation, Incognito exclusion, realtime failure followed by batch cleanup, and frozen rules edited during capture. Separate native Codex children provide controlled responses; the real production transport, callback, scheduler and completion owner perform the work. The [scheduler comparison](../../../mluva-workflows/tests/fixtures/segment-cleanup-evidence.md) independently checks 23 sessions and 26 projections, including ordered publication, queue limits, deadlines and late-result rejection.

| Independently released transaction | Checked result |
| --- | --- |
| Batch success, blank speech and provider failure | Preparation/recording/processing/terminal UI, deterministic rules, stored fallback title, full workflow result and success/failure audio retention |
| Preparation cancellation and recording Escape | No microphone before readiness, erased local audio, exact cancellation message, one terminal callback and owned process reaping |
| Repeated stop and rules edited during capture | No second dispatch, Escape refused during processing and frozen transcript preparation retained |
| Incognito success, failure and Escape | No History or diagnostics, memory-only staging erased and no retained audio |
| Realtime committed speech | Volatile partial text remains preview-only; final committed speech, exact PCM/commit messages and complete workflow result match |
| Realtime startup/stream failure | Explicit batch fallback route/reason, exact uploaded WAV and terminal UI match |
| Realtime recording cancellation | Already-sent audio is acknowledged, local audio is erased and socket workers and microphone are reaped |

The original seventeen transactions provide 81 actual GTK observations and remain unchanged. Every observed status/title/callout/tooltip, record label/icon/style/sensitivity, live preview, output and conversation identity matches the release. Full results and SQLite rows match after normalizing only generated identifiers, paths, timestamps and measured durations. Retention and protocol bytes are compared separately. Ten-millisecond GLib pulses continue during delayed HTTP/WebSocket/local processing, and callbacks and delivery remain on the owning GTK thread.

The comparison caught two native integration failures before repair. Completed Dictation did not save the released local fallback title, and Escape attached to the capture page missed an Incognito recording with focus at the window root. The controller now applies the existing generated-title compare-and-set and binds its key controller to the actual root while respecting visible dialogs and child handlers. The final owner passes all 17 transactions and 81 observations.

Two additional native fault transactions exercise cleanup rather than adding released UI comparisons. Incognito Notes preserves its acceptance text while erasing memory-backed audio, retaining no audio path or History and reaping its native janitor. Closing the controller while an actual HTTP request is pending synchronously invalidates completion: no callback, History row or late clipboard write occurs. Cancellation disables realtime submission before microphone draining and accounts for sent bytes after the transport workers finish. A separate ordinary audio test delays a real EOF consumer and verifies that cancellation keeps the async timer running, erases the private WAV and reaps the exact PCM process. Concurrent realtime cancellation callers both await transport cleanup. A further actual WebSocket fault test drops finalization after the peer receives Close while a real preview consumer is still pending. It failed with a stranded cleanup acknowledgement before repair; runtime-owned cleanup now outlives that request and both later cancellation callers finish.

A third native fault closes the controller during a real Stop drain with two active gated cleanup attempts. It observes the socket's Close before triggering exit and independently requires all three Codex children/workspaces to be gone after 600 ms, with no callback, History or clipboard mutation. The control failed because the active drain ignored exit until its deadline. The capture owner now prioritizes cancellation at that wait and awaits attempt cleanup. All 46 released transactions and three native faults pass after the repair.

The private runner creates separate display, session/accessibility buses, HOME/XDG, network/PID/mount namespaces and memory-backed `/dev/shm`; input, audio and GPU devices are masked. GTK 4.22.4 and Pango 1.58.2 are recorded and checked. Escape and clipboard canaries use private X11 helpers only. No real microphone, host input, visible desktop, provider account, managed credential or user content is touched. Temporary reference collectors, raw logs and failed comparisons remain under ignored `tmp/`.

```sh
cargo build --locked -p mluva-audio --bins -p mluva-providers --bins
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/native-capture-session -- bash -c '
  export PATH="$OFFSCREEN_SESSION_ROOT/codex-peer-tools:$PATH"
  export TZ=UTC
  exec cargo test --locked -p mluva-gtk --test capture_lifecycle -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
'
```

This proves joined batch/ElevenLabs realtime/compatible/local capture and realtime segment cleanup through synthetic PCM and real local transports. [Local preview sessions](../../../mluva-providers/tests/fixtures/local-preview-evidence.md) separately compare worker reuse, partials, active Stop and failure boundaries. The GTK local cases use sub-chunk audio, so they establish finalized capture integration, not Live preview scheduling or physical CPU/GPU recognition. The test builds a private Codex executable adapter first on its isolated PATH; it never changes the host environment or adds a production hook. The later [Live owner](live-evidence.md) adds bounded scheduling/revision/final-reconciliation/continuation checks and reruns this entire capture owner. Complete provider/service assembly, Live/Grilling/compatible/local workflows, picker waiting, review/meeting/archive owners, complete settings/welcome, global keys/widget, actual microphone and other-platform acceptance remain pending. Page pixels/scales, packaging, final Python removal and whole-app performance are not established. Every complete-workflow acceptance row remains Pending; the installed app/widget remain 1.6.0 and the full Rust goal stays active.
